From 26d92e951fe0a44ee4aec157cabb65a818cc8151 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Cong Wang <xiyou.wangcong@gmail.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Jan 2019 23:45:26 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] smc: move unhash as early as possible in smc_release()

In smc_release() we release smc->clcsock before unhash the smc
sock, but a parallel smc_diag_dump() may be still reading
smc->clcsock, therefore this could cause a use-after-free as
reported by syzbot.

Reported-and-tested-by: syzbot+fbd1e5476e4c94c7b34e@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Fixes: 51f1de79ad8e ("net/smc: replace sock_put worker by socket refcounting")
Cc: Ursula Braun <ubraun@linux.ibm.com>
Signed-off-by: Cong Wang <xiyou.wangcong@gmail.com>
Reported-by: syzbot+0bf2e01269f1274b4b03@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Reported-by: syzbot+e3132895630f957306bc@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/net/smc/af_smc.c b/net/smc/af_smc.c
index c4da4a78d369..c4e56602e0c6 100644
--- a/net/smc/af_smc.c
+++ b/net/smc/af_smc.c
@@ -146,6 +146,9 @@ static int smc_release(struct socket *sock)
 		sock_set_flag(sk, SOCK_DEAD);
 		sk->sk_shutdown |= SHUTDOWN_MASK;
 	}
+
+	sk->sk_prot->unhash(sk);
+
 	if (smc->clcsock) {
 		if (smc->use_fallback && sk->sk_state == SMC_LISTEN) {
 			/* wake up clcsock accept */
@@ -170,7 +173,6 @@ static int smc_release(struct socket *sock)
 		smc_conn_free(&smc->conn);
 	release_sock(sk);
 
-	sk->sk_prot->unhash(sk);
 	sock_put(sk); /* final sock_put */
 out:
 	return rc;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `net/smc/af_smc.c`**
- The call to `sk->sk_prot->unhash(sk);` has been moved from after the check for `smc->clcsock` to immediately after setting the socket as dead (`sock_set_flag(sk, SOCK_DEAD);`). 
- The previous call to `sk->sk_prot->unhash(sk);` at the end of the function has been removed.

### Relationships
The modification addresses a potential use-after-free bug by ensuring that the socket is unhashed before it is released. This change prevents a race condition where a parallel operation (`smc_diag_dump()`) could access the socket after it has been released, thus avoiding the risk of dereferencing a freed memory. The patch effectively moves the unhashing operation earlier in the `smc_release()` function to enhance safety and stability.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
sock_release(smc->clcsock);
sk->sk_prot->unhash(sk);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because `sock_release(smc->clcsock)` is called before `sk->sk_prot->unhash(sk)`, which releases the socket and allows `smc_diag_dump()` to access `smc->clcsock` after it has been freed, leading to a use-after-free condition.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
sk->sk_prot->unhash(sk);
sock_release(smc->clcsock);
```
Reason:
The patch moves the `sk->sk_prot->unhash(sk)` statement before `sock_release(smc->clcsock)`, ensuring that the socket is unhashed before it is released. This prevents any parallel access to `smc->clcsock` after it has been freed, thus eliminating the race condition and the potential use-after-free scenario.
